properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: SHA-1 implementation shipped by declared dependency crypto-js@^3.1.9-1 (nxt/html/www/js/package.json), vendored under nxt/html/www/js/crypto/3rdparty/cryptojs. Changeable here — migrate to SHA-2/3 usage.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The NRS client's entire account-key/signing/ECDH stack, browser-side: Curve25519 keygen derives account public keys from secret phrases, the deterministic EC-KCDSA sign/verify signs transactions locally and verifies them, and the curve25519_ X25519 ladder agrees message-encryption keys. All Shor-vulnerable; the scheme itself is fixed by the Nxt/Ardor chain protocol, so migration means a protocol hard fork — observable and fixable in the client only alongside a chain-wide change.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two natures, both real: nine sites are the vendored crypto-js HmacSHA256/384/512 surface shipped to browsers with the NRS client bundle; two are live — nxt/crypto/Scrypt.java:42/180 use JCA Mac "HmacSHA256" as the PRF inside the scrypt implementation that backs the SCRYPT minting hash function.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored crypto-js PBKDF2 module surface (bundle copy, standalone module, AMD registry, and bower/npm manifest entries). No NRS application call site found — the client derives message keys via Curve25519 ECDH + SHA-256 — but the KDF ships in the bundle; note CryptoJS.PBKDF2 defaults to a single iteration if any consumer ever calls it without raising cfg.iterations.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the core hash of the NXT/Ardor chain (transaction/block fullhashes, signing payloads). Not Shor-relevant; Grover-adequate at 256 bits. No action needed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The AES-GCM chain behind Nxt "encrypted to public key" (prunable anonymous) data: keys come from Curve25519 ECDH shared secrets (Crypto.getSharedKey), IVs are fresh SecureRandom bytes, and the ciphertext lands in on-chain attachments — data at rest that stays decryptable only under this scheme.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Nxt's SHA-3 exposure: Crypto.sha3() returns BouncyCastle Keccak.Digest256 (the pre-FIPS Keccak-256 padding variant, not SHA3-256 proper), and HashFunction registers SHA3 and Keccak25 among the accepted proof-of-work hash algorithms for mintable child currencies (CurrencyMinting).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Scrypt as a selectable proof-of-work hash for minting Nxt child currencies: HashFunction.SCRYPT is one of the accepted minting algorithms; the implementation is the vendored nxt.crypto.Scrypt (PBKDF2/HMAC-SHA256-based internally).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory entry: AES shipped via declared crypto-js@^3.1.9-1; NRS uses CryptoJS AES for local wallet/note encryption (nrs.encryption.js). Note crypto-js 3.x AES defaults to CBC with PKCS7 — actual mode is set per call site (covered by the app-side encryption objects).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The node's CSPRNG: JCA SecureRandom via ThreadLocal (Crypto.java:43-47), used for AES-GCM/CBC IVs (Crypto.java:204/224) and EncryptedData nonces. Default nxt.useStrongSecureRandom=false (nxt-default.properties:756) selects new SecureRandom() rather than getInstanceStrong() — still a CSPRNG, chosen to avoid /dev/random blocking. JS-side IVs use window.crypto.getRandomValues or Node crypto.randomBytes (nrs.encryption.js:803-820), both CSPRNGs. No weakness; no PQ action.

components.name: Java JSSE sessions on default settings (JDK version unknown)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Outbound TLS on JSSE defaults — the key exchange is ECDHE/DHE on any modern JDK (harvest-now-decrypt-later). Sites at APIRemoteConnector.java:45-46, MintWorker.java:237-238 and DesktopApplication.java:231-232 install TrustAllSSLProvider (certificate validation OFF) when trustRemoteCertificate is set — documented in nxt-default.properties:694 ("mint worker accepts any SSL"). JDK/Jetty version not pinned in the repo; PQ capability depends on the runtime JDK.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js 3.1.9 vendored into the NRS frontend and loaded by nrs.encryption.js (CryptoJS.AES.encrypt at nrs.encryption.js:671) — it IS the app's working crypto library, not a dormant header set. Its lib.WordArray.random (core.js:297-331) is Math.random-seeded and NOT a CSPRNG, though no NRS call site uses it (IVs come from getRandomBytes). PQ-capable: no. Changeable here.
